translations.text: And Moab rebelled against Israel after Ahab died.

And Ahaziah fell from the latticework of his upper room in Samaria and became ill. He sent messengers and said to them, “Go and consult Baal-zebub, the god of Ekron, to find out whether I will recover from this illness.” And they went to consult him.

And the angel of the Lord called Elijah the Tishbite and said, “Get up, go to meet the messengers of Ahaziah, king of Samaria, and say to them, ‘Is it because there is no God in Israel that you are going to consult Baal-zebub, the god of Ekron?’
“‘No, but this is what the Lord says: You will not come down from the bed you have gone up to, but you will certainly die there.’” And Elijah went and spoke to them.
And the messengers returned to him, and he said to them, “Why have you returned?”

And they said to him, “A man came to meet us and said to us, ‘Go back to the king who sent you and say to him: This is what the Lord says: Is it because there is no God in Israel that you are going to consult Baal-zebub, the god of Ekron? No, but you will not come down from the bed you have gone up to; you will certainly die.’”
And he spoke to them and said, “What did the man look like who came to meet you and spoke these words to you?”
And they said to him, “He was a hairy man, with a leather belt around his waist.” And he said, “That is Elijah the Tishbite.”

And he sent to him a captain of fifty with his fifty men. He went up and came to him, and Elijah was sitting on the top of the mountain. The captain of fifty spoke and said to him, “Man of God, the king has summoned you. Come down from there.”

Elijah answered and said to the captain of fifty, “If I am a man of God, let fire come down from heaven and consume you and your fifty men.” And fire came down from heaven and consumed him and his fifty men.

And the king again sent to him another captain of fifty with his fifty men. He went up, and the captain of fifty spoke and said to him, “Man of God, this is what the king says: Come down from there at once.”
Elijah answered him, saying, “If I am a man of God, let fire come down from heaven and consume you and your fifty men.” And fire from God came down from heaven and consumed him and his fifty men.

The king again sent a third captain of fifty with his fifty men. The third captain went up to Elijah, fell on his knees before him, pleaded with him, and said, “Man of God, let my life and the lives of these fifty servants of yours be precious in your sight.”
“For look, fire came down from heaven and consumed the first two captains of fifty and their fifty men. Now let the lives of your servants be precious in your eyes.”
And the angel of the Lord spoke to Elijah and said, “Go down with him, and do not be afraid of them.” And Elijah got up and went down with him to the king.

And he spoke to him and said, “Because you sent messengers to consult Baal-zebub, the god of Ekron, as though there were no God in Israel to consult—is that not so?—you will not come down from the bed you have gone up to, but you will certainly die.”

And he died according to the word of the Lord that Elijah had spoken. And Jehoram son of Ahab reigned over Israel in Samaria for twelve years, beginning in the eighteenth year of Jehoshaphat king of Judah. He did evil before the Lord, but not like his brothers or his mother. And he removed the pillars of Baal that his father had made and shattered them. Nevertheless, he clung to the sins of the house of Jeroboam, who had caused Israel to sin, and did not turn away from them. And the Lord became fiercely angry with the house of Ahab. And Jehoram his brother became king in his place in the second year of Jehoram king of Judah, son of Jehoshaphat, because he had no son.
And the rest of the acts of Ahaziah and everything he did—are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
And when the Lord was about to take Elijah up to heaven in a whirlwind, Elijah and Elisha went from Gilgal.
And Elijah said to Elisha, “Stay here, for the Lord has sent me to Bethel.” And Elisha said, “As the Lord lives, and as you live, I will not leave you.” And they came to Bethel.
The sons of the prophets who were in Bethel came out to Elisha and said to him, “Do you know that today the Lord is taking your master away from over your head?” He said, “I know too. Be silent.”
Elijah said to Elisha, “Stay here, for the Lord has sent me to Jericho.” He said, “As the Lord lives and as you live, I will not leave you.” So they came to Jericho.
The sons of the prophets who were in Jericho approached Elisha and said to him, “Do you know that today the Lord is taking your master away from over your head?” He said, “I know too. Be silent.”
Elijah said to him, “Stay here, for the Lord has sent me to the Jordan.” Elisha said, “As the Lord lives and as you live, I will not leave you.” So the two of them went on.
Fifty men from the sons of the prophets stood opposite them at a distance, while the two of them stood on the bank of the Jordan.
Elijah took his cloak, folded it, and struck the water. The water divided to one side and the other, and the two of them crossed on dry ground.
When they had crossed, Elijah said to Elisha, “Ask what I should do for you before I am taken away from you.” Elisha said, “Let a double portion of your spirit be upon me.”
Elijah said, “You have asked a difficult thing. But if you see me being taken up from you, it will be so; otherwise, it will not.”
As they went on, walking and talking, suddenly fiery chariots and fiery horses appeared and separated the two of them. Elijah was taken up into heaven amid a shaking.
Elisha watched and cried out, “Father, father! The chariots of Israel and its horsemen!” He saw him no more. He seized his clothes and tore them into two pieces.
Elisha took Elijah’s cloak, which he had thrown over him. Elisha returned and stood on the bank of the Jordan.

He took Elijah’s cloak, which he had thrown over him, struck the waters, and said, “Where are you, Lord, God of Elijah, [?]?” He struck the waters, and they divided to one side and the other, and Elisha crossed.

When the sons of the prophets who were in Jericho, opposite him, saw him, they said, “The spirit of Elijah has rested upon Elisha.” They came to meet him and bowed down to him with their faces to the ground.

They said to him, “Look, among your servants there are fifty strong men. Let them go and search for your master. Perhaps the Spirit of the Lord has taken him and cast him beside the Jordan, or onto one of the mountains, or onto one of the hills.” Elisha said, “Do not send them.”
They pressed him until he was embarrassed, and he said, “Send them.” They sent fifty men, who searched for three days but did not find him.
They returned to him while he was staying in Jericho. Elisha said to them, “Did I not tell you not to go?”
The men of the city said to Elisha, “Look, the location of this city is good, as you yourself, my lord, can see, but the water is bad and the land is barren.”
Elisha said, “Bring me a new jar and put [?] in it.” They brought it to him.
Elisha went out to the springs of water, threw salt there, and said, “Thus says the Lord: I heal these waters. No longer will death or barrenness come from them.”
The waters have remained healed to this day, according to the word that Elisha spoke.
He went up from there to Bethel. As he was going up along the road, little children came out of the city, shouting at him and saying, “Go up, baldhead! Go up, baldhead!”
He turned around, saw them, and cursed them in the name of the Lord, saying, “Sons of transgression and emptiness!” Two bears came out of the forest and tore apart forty-two of the children.
He went from there to Mount Carmel, and from there he returned to Samaria.
Jehoram son of Ahab became king over Israel in Samaria in the eighteenth year of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, and he reigned for twelve years.
He did evil in the sight of the Lord, but not like his father or his mother, and he destroyed his statues that his father had made.
Nevertheless, he clung to the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who had caused Israel to sin, and did not turn away from them.
Mesha king of Moab was a sheep breeder, and he paid the king of Israel a tribute of one hundred thousand ewes and one hundred thousand rams with their fleece.
After Ahab died, the king of Moab rebelled against the king of Israel.
King Joram went out from Samaria that day and mustered Israel.

He went and sent word to Jehoshaphat king of Judah, saying, “The king of Moab has rebelled against me. Will you go with me to war against Moab?” He said, “I will go. I am as you are, my troops are as your troops, and my horses are as your horses.”
He said, “By which road shall I go up?” He answered, “By the road through the wilderness of Edom.”
The king of Israel, the king of Judah, and the king of Edom went and made a roundabout journey of seven days. There was no water for the army or for the livestock that were with them.
The king of Israel said, “Alas! The Lord has trapped these three kings who have come here, to hand them over to Moab.”

Jehoshaphat said, “Is there no prophet of the Lord here, through whom we may inquire of the Lord?” One of the king of Israel’s servants answered, “Elisha son of Shaphat is here, who used to pour water on Elijah’s hands.”
Jehoshaphat said, “The word of the Lord is with him.” So the king of Israel, Jehoshaphat king of Judah, and the king of Edom went down to him.

Elisha said to the king of Israel, “What have I to do with you? Go to your father’s prophets and your mother’s prophets.” The king of Israel said to him, “Could it be that the Lord has called these three kings here to hand them over to Moab?”
Elisha said, “As the Lord of hosts lives, before whom I stand, if I did not have regard for Jehoshaphat king of Judah, I would not even look at you or see you.”
“But now bring me a psalm singer.” When the psalm singer played, the hand of the Lord came upon him.
He said, “This is what the Lord says: Make this valley full of pits.”
For thus says the Lord: “You will see no wind and no rain, yet this ravine will be filled with water, and you, your livestock, and your beasts of burden will drink.”
“This is an easy thing in the Lord’s sight, and I will hand Moab over to you.”
“You will strike every fortified city and every choice city. You will cut down every good tree, stop up every spring of water, and ruin every good field with stones.”
In the morning, when the sacrifice was offered, water came from the direction of Edom, and the land was filled with water.
All Moab heard that the kings had come up to fight against them. Everyone old enough to put on a sword belt, and everyone older, came out and stood at the border. They rose early in the morning.
The sun shone on the water, and the Moabites saw the water opposite them, red like blood.
They said, “That is blood shed by the sword! The kings have fought one another, and each has struck down his companion. Now, Moab, on to the plunder!”
They entered Israel’s camp, but the Israelites rose and struck the Moabites, who fled before them. The Israelites kept advancing and striking the Moabites.

They destroyed the cities. Each man threw his stone into every good field, filling it with stones. They stopped up every spring of water and cut down every good tree, until only the stones of the demolished walls were left. The slingers surrounded it and struck it.
When the king of Moab saw that the battle was too strong for him, he took seven hundred swordsmen with him to break through to the king of Edom, but they could not.

The king took his firstborn son, whom he had made king in his place, and offered him as a burnt offering on the wall. Great remorse came upon Israel, and they withdrew from him and returned to their own land.

A woman, the wife of one of the sons of the prophets, cried out to Elisha, saying, “Your servant, my husband, has died, and you yourself know that your servant feared the Lord. Now the creditor has come to take my two sons as his slaves.”
Elisha said to her, “What shall I do for you? Tell me what you have in your house.” She said, “Your servant has nothing at all in the house except oil with which we anoint ourselves.”
He said to her, “Go and ask all your neighbors for empty vessels, and do not get only a few.
Then go inside and shut the door behind you and your sons. Pour into all the vessels until they are full, and set them aside.”
She went away from him and shut the door behind herself and her sons. They brought the vessels to her, and she poured.
When the vessels were full, she said to her sons, “Bring me another vessel.” They said to her, “There is no other vessel.” Then the oil stopped.
She went and told the man of God, and Elisha said, “Go, sell the oil and pay your interest. You and your sons shall live on the remaining oil.”
One day Elisha passed through Shunem. A prominent woman was there, and she persuaded him to eat bread. After that, whenever he went there, he would stop to eat and drink.
The woman said to her husband, “I know that this man of God is holy, and his route passes by our home.”
“Let us make a small upstairs room for him and put a bed, a table, a chair, and a lampstand in it. Then, whenever he comes to us, he can go in there.”
One day he came there, entered the upper room, and slept there.
He said to Gehazi, his servant, “Call that Shunammite woman to me.” He called her, and she stood before him.

He said to the servant, “Say to her, ‘You have made all these arrangements for us. What should be done for you? Do you have some matter to bring before the king or the commander of the army?’” She said, “I live among my own people.”
He said, “What should be done for her?” Gehazi, his servant, said, “Indeed, that would be very good, for she has no son, and her husband is not at all old.”
He said, “Call her.” He called her, and she stood at the door.
Elisha said to her, “At this time, at this same season, you will hold a child in your arms.” She said, “No, my lord, man of God! Do not lie to your servant.”
The woman conceived and bore a son at that time, while she was still alive, as Elisha had told her.
The child grew strong, and it happened that he went out to his father among the reapers.
He said to his father, “My head! My head!” His father said to the servant, “Take him to his mother.”
He took him to his mother, and the child lay on her knees until noon and died.
She carried him upstairs and laid him on the bed of the man of God, shut the door behind him, and went out.
She called her husband and said, “Send me one of the servants and one of the donkeys, so that I may hurry to the man of God and return.”
He said, “Why are you going to him today? It is neither the new moon nor the Sabbath.” She said, “All is well.”
She saddled the donkey and said to her servant, “Drive it and go. Do not hold back at all from going on with it, unless I tell you, ‘Come here’; then come.”
And go to the man of God on Mount Carmel. When Elisha saw her coming toward him, he said to Gehazi, his servant, “There is that Shunammite woman.
Run to meet her and say, ‘Is all well with you? Is all well with your husband? Is all well with the child?’” She said, “All is well.”

She came to Elisha on the mountain and took hold of his feet. Gehazi approached to push her away, but Elisha said, “Leave her alone, for she is deeply distressed. The Lord has hidden it from me and has not told me.”
She said, “Did I ask my lord for a son? Did I not say, ‘Do not deceive me’?”

Elisha said to Gehazi, “Put a belt around your waist, take my staff in your hand, and go. If you meet anyone, do not greet him, and if anyone greets you, do not answer him. Lay my staff on the child’s face.”
The child's mother said, “As the Lord lives and as you live, I will not leave you.” So Elisha got up and followed her.
Gehazi went ahead of them and laid the staff on the child’s face, but there was no sound and no response. He returned to meet Elisha and reported to him, saying, “The child has not awakened.”
Elisha entered the house, and there was the child, dead and lying on his bed.
Elisha entered the house, shut the door behind the two of them, and prayed to the Lord.
He went up and lay on the child, placing his mouth on the child's mouth, his eyes on the child's eyes, and his hands on the child's hands. He bent over him, and the child's body grew warm.
He turned back and walked to and fro in the house. Then he went up and covered the child seven times, and the child opened his eyes.
Elisha called to Gehazi and said, “Call the Shunammite woman here.” He called her, and she came in to him. Elisha said, “Take your son.”
The woman came in, fell at his feet, and bowed to the ground before him. Then she took her son and went out.

Elisha returned to Gilgal. There was a famine in the land, and the sons of the prophets were sitting before him. Elisha said to his young servant, “Put the large pot on and cook stew for these sons of the prophets.”

He went out into the field to gather herbs and found a vine in the field. He gathered a full backload of unripe grapes from it, came back, and put them into the stew pot, for he did not know what they were.
He served it to the men to eat. As they ate the stew, they cried out and said, “There is death in this pot, man of God!” And they could not eat it.
He said, “Bring flour and put it into that pot.” Then Elisha said to Gehazi, his young servant, “Serve it to the people, and let them eat.” And there was nothing harmful in the pot.
A man came from Baal-shalishah and brought the man of God bread from the first harvested crops: barley loaves and cakes of dried fruit in a sack. He said, “Give it to the people, and let them eat.”
His servant said, “How can I set this before a hundred men?” He said, “Give it to the people, and let them eat, for this is what the Lord says: ‘They will eat and have some left over.’”
He set it before them, and they ate and left some over, according to the word of the Lord.

Naaman, commander of the Syrian army, was a great man in his master's eyes and highly regarded, because through him the Lord had given victory to the Syrians. The man was a mighty warrior, but he had leprosy.
The Syrians went out lightly armed and captured a little girl from the land of Israel. She served Naaman's wife.
She said to her mistress, “If only my master would go before the prophet of God who is in Samaria! He would then cure him of his leprosy.”
He went in and told his master, saying, “This is what the girl from the land of Israel said.”
The king of Syria said to Naaman, “Go, and I will send a letter to the king of Israel.” So he went, taking with him ten talents of silver, six thousand gold coins, and ten sets of clothing.
He carried a letter to the king of Israel, which read as follows: “Now, when this letter reaches you, know that I have sent my servant Naaman to you, so that you may cure him of his leprosy.”

When the king of Israel read the letter, he tore his clothes and said, “Am I God, able to kill or give life, that he has sent to me to cleanse this man of his leprosy? But understand and see that he is seeking a pretext against me.”

When Elisha, the man of God, heard that the king of Israel had torn his clothes, he sent word to the king of Israel, saying, “Why have you torn your clothes? Let Naaman come to me, and he will know that there is a prophet in Israel.”
Naaman came with horses and chariots and stopped at the door of Elisha's house.
Elisha sent a messenger to him, saying, “Go and wash seven times in the Jordan, and your flesh will be restored and you will be clean.”
Naaman became angry and went away, saying, “I thought he would come out to me, stand there, call on the name of the Lord his God, place his hand over the affected spot, and cure the leprosy.”
“Are not Abana and Pharpar, the rivers of Damascus, better than all the waters of Israel? Why should I not go and wash in them and become clean?” He turned and went away in anger.

His servants approached and spoke to him, saying, “Father, if the prophet had told you to do something difficult, would you not have had to do it? How much more, then, when he said, ‘Wash and be clean’?”
Naaman went down and dipped himself in the Jordan seven times, according to Elisha’s word. His flesh became like the flesh of a young child, and he was clean.
He returned to Elisha with his entire company, came and stood before him, and said, “Now I know that there is no God anywhere on earth except in Israel. So now, accept a gift from your servant.”
Elisha said, “As the Lord lives, before whom I stand, I will accept nothing.” Naaman urged him to accept it, but he would not agree.

Naaman said, “Since you will not, let your servant be given two mule-loads of earth from this land, for your servant will no longer offer burnt offerings or sacrifices to foreign gods, but only to the Lord.

May the Lord forgive your servant in this matter: when my master enters the house of Rimmon to bow down there, and he leans on my arm, I also bow down in the house of Rimmon. When he bows down in the house of Rimmon, may the Lord forgive your servant for this.”
Elisha said to Naaman, “Go in peace.” And he went away from him, leaving the land of Israel.

Gehazi, Elisha’s young servant, said, “My master has spared this Naaman the Syrian by not accepting from his hand anything he brought. As the Lord lives, I will run after him and take something from him.”
Gehazi hurried after Naaman. Naaman saw him running after him and turned from his chariot to meet him. He said, “Is all well?”

Gehazi said, “All is well. My master sent me to you, saying, ‘Two young men from the sons of the prophets have just come to me from the hill country of Ephraim. Give them a talent of silver and two changes of clothes.’”

Naaman said, “If that is so, take three talents of silver.” He pressed him to accept them, tied up three talents of silver in two bags, along with two changes of clothes, and gave them to two of his servants, who carried them ahead of Gehazi.
They came to the dark place, and he took the things from their hands and put them in the house. He sent the men away, and they left.
He went in and stood before his master. Elisha said to him, “Where have you come from, Gehazi?” Gehazi said, “Your servant has not gone either this way or that.”

Elisha said to him, “Did not my heart go with you when the man turned from his chariot to meet you? And now you have taken the silver and the clothes for olive groves, vineyards, cattle, sheep, male servants, and female servants.
Naaman’s leprosy will cling to you and your descendants forever.” And Gehazi went out from his presence with leprosy white as snow.
The sons of the prophets said to Elisha, “Look, the place where we live is too cramped for us.”
“Let us go to the Jordan, and let each man take a beam from there, and let us make a dwelling for ourselves there.” He said, “Go.”
One of them said, “Please come along with your servants too.” He said, “I will come.”
He went with them, and they came to the Jordan and began cutting wood.
As one of them was felling a tree trunk, the iron blade fell into the water. He cried out and said, “Oh, master! It was borrowed!”
The man of God said, “Where did it fall?” He showed him the place. Then he split a piece of wood and threw it there, and the iron rose to the surface.
He said, “Lift it out for yourself.” And he stretched out his hand and took it.
The king of Syria was waging war against Israel. He consulted with his servants and said, “I will camp in ambush at such-and-such a place.”
Elisha sent word to the king of Israel, saying, “Be careful not to pass through that place, because the Syrians are hiding there.”
The king of Israel sent men to the place Elisha had told him about and had it checked for ambushes, and he took precautions against it—not just once or twice.
The king of Syria was enraged over this matter. He summoned his servants and said to them, “Will you not tell me who is betraying me to the king of Israel?”
One of his servants said, “No, my lord the king. Rather, Elisha, the prophet in Israel, tells the king of Israel everything you say in your bedroom.”
He said, “Go and find out where he is, so that I may send men to capture him.” They reported to him, saying, “He is in Dothan.”
He sent chariots, horses, and a large army there. They came by night and surrounded the city.
He rose early to attend to Elisha and went out. There was an army surrounding the city, with horses and chariots. The young man said to him, “Master, what shall we do?”
Elisha said, “Do not be afraid, for those with us are more numerous than those with them.”
Elisha prayed and said, “Lord, open this young man’s eyes so that he may see.” The Lord opened his eyes, and he saw that the mountain was full of horses and fiery chariots all around Elisha.
They came down to him, and Elisha prayed to the Lord and said, “Strike these people with blindness.” He struck them with blindness, as Elisha had asked.
Elisha said to them, “This is not the road, and this is not the city. Follow me, and I will take you to the man you are seeking.” He led them to Samaria.
When he entered Samaria, Elisha said, “Lord, open their eyes so that they may see.” The Lord opened their eyes, and they saw that they were in the middle of Samaria.
When the king of Israel saw them, he said to Elisha, “Shall I strike them down, father?”

He said, “Do not strike them down. You may strike down only those whom you capture with your own sword and bow. Set bread and water before these men, so that they may eat and drink and return to their master.”
He set fodder before them in a large [?], and they ate and drank. He sent them away, and they went to their master. The Syrian raiding parties no longer came into the land of Israel.
After this, Ben-hadad, king of Syria, gathered his whole army, marched up, and laid siege to Samaria.
There was a great famine in Samaria. They besieged it until a donkey’s skull cost fifty shekels of silver, and a quarter of a kab of dove’s dung cost fifty-five pieces of silver.
The king of Israel was walking along the wall, and a woman cried out to him, saying, “Save me, my lord the king!”
He said, “May the Lord not save you! From where can I save you—from the threshing floor or from the winepress?”
The king said to her, “What is the matter with you?” She said, “This woman said to me, ‘Give your son, and we will eat him today; we will eat my son tomorrow.’”
“So we boiled my son and ate him. On the second day I said to her, ‘Give your son, and we will eat him.’ But she hid her son.”
When the king heard the woman’s words, he tore his clothes. As he was walking along the wall, the people saw the sackcloth he wore underneath, against his body.
He said, “May God do such and such to me, and add such and such, if the head of Elisha son of Shaphat remains on him today!”

Elisha was sitting in his house, and the elders were sitting with him. The king sent a man ahead of him. Before the messenger reached him, Elisha said to the elders, “Do you know that this son of a murderer has sent someone to take off my head? When the messenger comes in, hold him at the doors. Is not the sound of his master’s footsteps behind him?”
While he was still speaking with them, the messenger came down to them and said, “This calamity is from the Lord. Why should I wait for the Lord any longer?”

Elisha said, “Hear the word of the Lord. This is what the Lord says: Tomorrow at this time, one seah of fine flour will cost one shekel, and two seahs of barley will cost one shekel, at the gates of Samaria.”

The officer on whose arm the king leaned answered Elisha, saying, “Even if the Lord were to make floodgates in heaven, could this happen?” Elisha said, “You will see it with your own eyes, but you will not eat any of it.”
There were four men with leprosy at the city gate, and they said to one another, “Why are we sitting here and dying?”

If we say, ‘Let us enter the city,’ there is famine in the city, and we will die there. And if we sit here, we will still die. So now, come, let us go to the camp of the Syrians. If they spare us, we will live, and if they kill us, we will die.
They rose at dawn to enter the camp of the Syrians. They came to one part of the Syrian camp, and there was no one there.

For the Lord had made the Syrian camp hear the rumbling of chariots and the sound of a great army. They said to one another, “Now the king of Israel has hired the kings of the Hittites and the kings of the Egyptians against us.”
They rose and fled in the darkness, leaving their tents, their horses, and their donkeys in the camp just as they were, and fled for their lives.

The lepers entered one part of the camp and went into a tent. They ate and drank, took silver, gold, and clothing from there, and went away and hid them. Then they returned, entered another tent, took things from there, and went away and hid them.

They said to one another, “What we are doing is not right. This day is a day of good news. Shall we remain silent and wait for the morning light? We will be found guilty. So now, come, let us go and report this to the king’s household.”

They went and called out at the city gate and reported to them, saying, “We entered the camp of the Syrians, and there was no one there and no human voice, but only horses tied up and donkeys tied up, and their tents were still standing just as they were.”
The gatekeepers called out and passed the news inside to the king’s household.

The king rose during the night and said to his servants, “I will tell you what the Syrians have done to us. They know that we are starving. They have left the camp and hidden outside, saying, ‘Perhaps they will come out of the city, and we will capture them alive, enter the city, and come out.’”
One of his servants answered, “Let them take five of the remaining horses that are left here from the whole population of Israel, now diminished [?], and let us send them there and see.”
They took two mounted horsemen, and the king sent them after the king of the Syrians, saying, “Go and see.”
They followed them as far as the Jordan, and the whole road was full of clothing and equipment that the Syrians had thrown away in their panic. The messengers returned and reported to the king.
The people went out and plundered the camp of the Syrians. A measure of fine flour sold for one shekel, and two measures of barley for a shekel, according to the word of the Lord.
The king appointed the officer on whose hand he leaned, and the people trampled him in the crowd at the gate, and he died, just as the man of God had said when the messenger came down to him.

It happened just as Elisha had told the king, saying, “Two measures of barley will sell for one shekel, and a measure of fine flour for a shekel. This will happen tomorrow at this time at the gates of Samaria.”

The officer had answered Elisha, saying, “Even if the Lord made floodgates in heaven, could what you say happen?” Elisha had said, “You will see it with your own eyes, but you will not eat any of it.”
And that is what happened to him: the people trampled him in the crowd at the gate, and he died.

Elisha spoke to the woman whose son he had restored to life, saying, “Rise, go to your house, and live as a foreigner wherever you can, for the Lord has called for a famine upon this land. Indeed, a famine has come upon the land for seven years.”
The woman rose and did according to Elisha’s word. She and her household went away and lived as foreigners in the land of the Philistines for seven years.
When the seven years were over, the woman returned from the land of the Philistines and came to appeal to the king concerning her house and her fields.
The king spoke with Gehazi, the servant of Elisha the man of God, and said, “Tell me all the great things Elisha has done.”

As he was telling the king how Elisha had brought the dead son back to life, the woman whose son Elisha had brought back to life appeared before him, appealing to the king about her house and her fields. Gehazi said, “My lord the king, this is the woman, and this is her son whom Elisha brought back to life.”

The king questioned the woman, and she told him. The king assigned her a eunuch and said, “Restore all her property to her, along with all the produce of the field from the day she left the country until now.”
Elisha came to Damascus, and Ben-hadad, king of the Syrians, was ill. He was told, “The man of God has come here.”
The king said to Hazael, “Take a gift with you and go to meet the man of God. Inquire of the Lord through him, saying, ‘Will I recover from this illness of mine?’”

Hazael went to meet him, taking a gift with him and all the fine things of Damascus, forty camel-loads. He went and stood before him and said, “Father Elisha, your son Ben-hadad, king of the Syrians, has sent me to you, saying, ‘Will I recover from this illness of mine?’”
Elisha said to him, “Go and tell him, ‘You will certainly recover.’ But the Lord has shown me that he will certainly die.”
He stood before him, ashamed, and the man of God wept.

Hazael said, “Why are you weeping, my lord?” He said, “I know what you will do to the Israelites: you will set their fortresses on fire, kill their chosen men with the sword, slaughter their children, and rip open their pregnant women.”
Hazael said, “Who is your servant, a mere dog, that he should do such a thing?” Elisha said, “The Lord has shown me that you will reign over the Syrians.”
Hazael left Elisha and went to his master, who said to him, “What did Elisha say?” He said, “He told me that you will certainly recover.”
The next day, he took a coverlet, soaked it in water, and spread it over his face, and he died. Hazael reigned in his place.
In the fifth year of Joram son of Ahab, king of Israel, Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, began to reign.
He was thirty-two years old when he began to reign, and he reigned eight years in Jerusalem.
He followed the ways of the kings of Israel, as the house of Ahab had done, because Ahab’s daughter was his wife. He did evil in the sight of the Lord.
But the Lord was unwilling to destroy Judah for the sake of his servant David, just as he had promised to give him and his sons a lamp forever.
In his days, Edom rebelled against Judah’s rule and appointed a king over itself.
Jehoram went to Zair with all his chariots. He rose early during the night and struck the Edomites who had surrounded him and the commanders of the chariots. The army fled, each to his own tent.
Edom rebelled against the rule of Judah and remains independent to this day. At that time Libnah also rebelled.
The rest of the acts of Jehoram and everything he did—are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah?
Jehoram rested with his ancestors and was buried with his ancestors in the city of David, his ancestor. His son Ahaziah reigned in his place.
In the twelfth year of Joram son of Ahab, king of Israel, Ahaziah son of Jehoram, king of Judah, began to reign.
Ahaziah was twenty-two years old when he began to reign, and he reigned one year in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Athaliah, daughter of Omri, king of Israel.
He followed the ways of the house of Ahab and did evil in the sight of the Lord, as the house of Ahab had done, because he was a son-in-law of the house of Ahab.
He went with Joram son of Ahab to war against Hazael king of the Syrians at Ramoth-gilead, and the Syrians wounded Joram.

King Joram returned to Jezreel to recover from the wounds the Syrians had inflicted on him at Ramoth when he fought against Hazael king of the Syrians. Ahaziah son of Jehoram, king of Judah, went down to Jezreel to see Joram son of Ahab, because he was ill.
Elisha the prophet called one of the sons of the prophets and said to him, “Fasten your belt, take this flask of oil in your hand, and go to Ramoth-gilead.
When you enter there, look for Jehu son of Jehoshaphat, son of Nimshi. Go in, have him rise from among his brothers, and take him into an inner room.
Take that flask of oil, pour it on his head, and say, ‘Thus says the Lord: I have anointed you king over Israel.’ Then open the door and flee; do not linger.”
The young prophet went to Ramoth-gilead.
He entered, and there were the commanders of the army sitting together. He said, “I have a message for you, commander.” Jehu said, “For which one of us?” He said, “For you, commander.”
Jehu rose and entered the room. The young prophet poured the oil on his head and said to him, “Thus says the Lord, the God of Israel: I have anointed you king over the Lord’s people, over Israel.

You shall destroy the house of Ahab your master from before you, and avenge the blood of my servants the prophets and the blood of all the Lord’s servants at the hands of Jezebel and her entire house.
You shall destroy everyone of Ahab’s house who urinates against a wall, both those confined and those left in Israel,
making Ahab’s house like the house of Jeroboam son of Nebat and like the house of Baasha son of Ahijah.
Dogs shall eat Jezebel in the territory of Jezreel, and there shall be no one to bury her.” Then he opened the door and fled.
Jehu went out to his master’s servants, and they said to him, “Is all well? Why did that madman come to you?” He said to them, “You yourselves know the man and his babbling.”
They said, “That is not true! Tell us.” Jehu said to them, “He spoke to me in these words, saying, ‘Thus says the Lord: I have anointed you king over Israel.’”
When they heard this, they hurried, and each took his cloak and placed it beneath him on one of the steps where they were sitting. They sounded the horn and said, “Jehu is king!”
Jehu son of Jehoshaphat, son of Nimshi, gathered troops against Joram. Joram himself and all Israel had been guarding Ramoth-gilead against Hazael king of the Syrians.

King Joram had returned to Jezreel to recover from the wounds the Syrians had inflicted on him when he fought against Hazael king of the Syrians. Jehu said, “If you are with me in spirit, let no fugitive leave this city to go and report it in Jezreel.”

Jehu mounted and went down to Jezreel, for Joram king of Israel was recovering in Jezreel from the arrow wounds inflicted on him at Ramoth when he fought against Hazael king of the Syrians, for he was strong and a mighty warrior, and he rested there. Ahaziah king of Judah had gone down to see Joram.
The watchman went up onto the tower of Jezreel and saw dust as Jehu approached. He said, “I see dust.” Joram said, “Take a horseman and send him to meet them, and let him ask, ‘Is all well?’”

The horseman went to meet him and said, “This is what the king says: ‘Is all well?’” Jehu said, “What have you to do with whether all is well? Turn around and follow me.” The lookout reported, saying, “The messenger has reached them, but he has not returned.”
He sent a second horseman, who said, “Thus says the king: ‘Is all well?’” Jehu said, “What have you to do with whether all is well? Turn around and follow me.”
The watchman reported, saying, “He reached them but did not return. The driving is like the driving of Jehu son of Nimshi, for he is approaching furiously.”

Joram said, “Harness the chariot!” They harnessed his chariot, and Joram king of Israel and Ahaziah king of Judah each mounted his own chariot. They went out to meet Jehu and found him on the plot of land belonging to Naboth the Jezreelite.
When Joram saw Jehu, he said, “Is there peace, Jehu?” Jehu said, “What peace can there be while the prostitution of your mother Jezebel and her sorceries continue to abound?”
Joram turned around and fled, saying to Ahaziah, “It is treachery, Ahaziah!”
Jehu [?] and struck Joram between his shoulders. The arrow went through his heart, and he collapsed onto his knees.

He said to Bidkar, his armor-bearer, “Throw him onto the plot in the field belonging to Naboth the Jezreelite. For I remember that when you and I were riding together behind Ahab his father, the Lord pronounced this oracle against him:

‘Surely I saw the blood of Naboth and the blood of his sons yesterday, says the Lord, and I will repay him on this plot of land, says the Lord.’ Now take him and throw him onto that plot, according to the word of the Lord.”

Ahaziah king of Judah saw this and fled along the road to Beth-haggan. Jehu pursued him relentlessly and said, “Come, him too!” He struck him in his chariot as he was going up the ascent of Bera, which is Ibleam. He fled to Megiddo and died there.
His servants carried him to Jerusalem and buried him in his tomb with his ancestors in the City of David.
In the eleventh year of Joram king of Israel, Ahaziah became king over Judah.
Jehu came to Jezreel. Jezebel heard about it, painted her eyes, adorned her head, and looked out through the window.
As Jehu entered the city, she said, “Is there peace, Zimri, murderer of your master?”
He lifted his face toward the window and said, “Who are you? Come down to me!” Two eunuchs looked down at him.
He said, “Throw her down!” They threw her down, and some of her blood splashed onto the wall and the horses, and they trampled her underfoot.
He went inside, ate and drank, and said, “See to that cursed woman and bury her, for she is a king’s daughter.”
They went to bury her, but they found nothing of her except her skull, her feet, and the palms of her hands.
They returned and told him, and he said, “This is the word of the Lord, which he spoke through Elijah the Tishbite, saying, ‘On the plot of land in Jezreel, dogs will eat the flesh of Jezebel,
and Jezebel’s corpse will be like dung on the surface of the field, on that plot of land, so that no one will be able to say, “This is Jezebel.”’”
Ahab had seventy sons in Samaria. Jehu wrote a letter and sent it to Samaria, to the rulers of Samaria, the elders, and the guardians of Ahab’s sons, saying:
“When this letter reaches you, your master’s sons are with you, and you have chariots and horses, fortified cities and weapons.
Choose the best and most upright of your master’s sons, establish him on his father’s throne, and fight for your master’s house.”
They were very afraid and said, “Look, the two kings could not stand against him. How can we stand against him?”

Those of the palace and the city, the elders, and the guardians sent word to Jehu, saying, “We are your servants, and we will do whatever you tell us. We will not make anyone king, but we will do whatever is good in your eyes.”

He wrote them a second letter, saying, “If you are on my side and obey my voice, take the heads of the men who are your master’s sons and bring them to me in Jezreel tomorrow at this same time.” The king’s sons numbered seventy men, and the leading men of the city were raising them.
When the letter reached them, they seized the king’s sons and killed all seventy men. They put their heads in baskets and sent them to him in Jezreel.
The messenger came and reported, “They have brought the heads of the king’s sons.” He said, “Put them in two heaps outside the city until morning.”
In the morning he went out, stood before all the people, and said, “You are innocent. Look, I rose against my master and killed him, but look at these—who slaughtered them [?]?”
“For none of the word of the Lord that the Lord spoke against the house of Ahab will fall to the ground. The Lord has done what he spoke through his servant Elijah.”
Jehu struck down everyone remaining of the house of Ahab in Jezreel, all his leading men, his acquaintances, and his priests, leaving him no survivor.
He set out and went to Samaria. While he was at Beth-eked of the shepherds along the way,
Jehu met the brothers of Ahaziah king of Judah and said, “Who are you?” They said, “We are Ahaziah’s brothers, and we have come down to greet the king’s sons and the queen’s sons.”
He said, “Take them alive.” They took them alive and slaughtered them at Beth-eked, forty-two men, leaving not one of them alive.

He went on from there and met Jehonadab son of Rechab coming toward him. He greeted him, and Jehu said to him, “Is your heart true, as my heart is toward yours?” Jehonadab said, “It is.” Jehu said, “If it is, give me your hand.” He gave him his hand, and Jehu brought him up beside him into the chariot.
He said to him, “Come with me and see my zeal for the Lord.” He seated him in his chariot.
He entered Samaria and struck down all who remained of Ahab’s house in Samaria, until he had destroyed them, according to the word of the Lord that he had spoken to Elijah.
Jehu gathered all the people and said to them, “Ahab served Baal a little; Jehu will serve him much.”

“Now summon to me all Baal’s prophets, all his servants, and his priests. Let no one be missing, for there will be a great sacrifice to Baal. Whoever is missing shall not live.” Jehu acted deceitfully in order to destroy Baal’s servants.
Jehu said, “Consecrate offerings to Baal.” And they made a proclamation.
Jehu sent throughout all Israel, and all Baal’s servants came. No one remained who did not come. They entered Baal’s temple, and Baal’s temple was filled from end to end.
Jehu said to the [?], “Bring out robes for all Baal’s servants.” They brought out the robes for them.

Jehu and Jehonadab son of Rechab entered the temple of Baal. He said to the servants of Baal, “Search and see whether any servants of the Lord are here among you. There must be only servants of Baal here.”

Jehu went in to offer incense and burnt offerings. Jehu stationed three hundred and eighty men outside and said, “If anyone lets one of the men whom I am handing over to you escape, his life shall be forfeited in place of that man’s life.”

When he had finished offering the burnt offerings, Jehu said to the runners and the armed men, “Go in and strike them down. Let none of them escape.” They struck them down with the edge of the sword. The runners and the armed men threw them out and went as far as the city of Baal’s temple.
They brought out the pillar of Baal’s temple and burned it.
They demolished Baal’s pillars, tore down Baal’s temple, and made it into washing places, which remain to this day.
Thus Jehu destroyed Baal out of Israel.
But Jehu did not turn away from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who had caused Israel to sin—from the golden calves at Bethel and Dan.

The Lord said to Jehu, “Because you have done well in doing what is right before me, and have done to the house of Ahab everything that was in my heart, your descendants shall sit on Israel’s throne to the fourth generation.”
But Jehu was not careful to walk in the law of the Lord, the God of Israel, with all his heart. He did not turn away from the sins of Jeroboam, who had caused Israel to sin.
In those days the Lord began to strike down throughout all the territory of Israel, and Hazael struck them throughout all the territory of Israel.
From the Jordan eastward, all the land of Gilead, of Gad, of Reuben, and of Manasseh, from Aroer, which is on the bank of the Arnon ravine, including Gilead and Bashan.
Now the rest of the acts of Jehu, everything he did, all his might, and all the forces he assembled—are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
Jehu slept with his fathers, and they buried him in Samaria. His son Jehoahaz reigned in his place.
The time Jehu reigned over Israel in Samaria was twenty-eight years.
When Athaliah, the mother of Ahaziah, saw that her sons were dead, she destroyed all the royal offspring.

But Jehosheba, the daughter of King Jehoram and sister of Ahaziah, took Joash, the son of Ahaziah, and stole him away from among the king’s sons who were being killed. She hid him and his nurse in a bedroom, out of Athaliah’s sight, and he was not killed.
He was hidden with her in the house of the Lord for six years, while Athaliah reigned over the land.

In the seventh year, Jehoiada sent for the commanders of hundreds, the Carites, and the runners, and brought them into the house of the Lord. He made the Lord’s covenant with them, and Jehoiada showed them the king’s son.
He gave them orders, saying, “This is what you are to do: a third of you are to come on duty at the beginning of the Sabbath and keep watch over the royal house at the gate,
a third at the gate of the roads, and a third at the gate behind the guards. You are to keep watch over the house.
The two divisions among you, all those going off duty at the beginning of the Sabbath, are to keep watch over the house of the Lord, guarding the house of the Lord near the king.
You are to surround the king, each man with his weapon in his hand. Whoever enters the ranks is to die.” And he was with the king when he went in and when he went out.

The commanders of hundreds did everything that Jehoiada the wise commanded. Each man took his men, those coming on duty at the beginning of the Sabbath together with those going off duty at the beginning of the Sabbath, and came to Jehoiada the priest.
The priest gave the commanders of hundreds the spears and all the weapons of King David that were in the house of the Lord.
The guards took their positions, each man with his weapon in his hand, from the right side of the house to the left side of the house, around the altar and the royal house.
He sent out the king’s son, placed the crown and the testimony upon him, made him king, and anointed him. He clapped his hands and said, “Long live the king!”
Athaliah heard the sound of the people running and went to the people in the house of the Lord.

She looked, and there he stood by the pillar according to his custom, with singers and trumpeters around the king. All the people of the land were rejoicing and sounding their trumpets. Athaliah tore her clothes and cried out, saying, “Treason! Treason!”

Jehoiada the priest gave orders to the commanders of hundreds who were officers of the army, saying to them, “Bring her out from within the ranks, and whoever follows her is to die by the sword.” For the priest had said, “She must not be killed in the house of the Lord.”
They laid hands on her and went along the horses’ entrance road to the king’s house, and she died there.
Jehoiada made a covenant between the Lord, the king, and the people, that they would be the Lord’s people, and also between the king and the people.

All the people of the land entered the house of Baal and demolished it. They shattered his altars and his images into small pieces and killed Mattan, the priest of Baal, before the altar. The priest stationed officers in the house of the Lord.

He took the commanders of hundreds, the Carites, the runners, and all the people of the land, and they brought the king down from the house of the Lord. He entered by the road through the runners’ gate into the royal house, and he seated him on the throne of the kings.
All the people of the land rejoiced, and the city was quiet. They killed Athaliah with the sword in the king’s house.
Joash was seven years old when he began to reign.
In the seventh year of Jehu, Joash became king, and he reigned forty years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Zibiah, from Beersheba.
Joash did what was right before the Lord throughout all the days when Jehoiada the priest instructed him.
But they did not abandon the high places, and the people still sacrificed and burned incense at the high places.

Joash said to the priests, “All the silver from sacred offerings brought into the house of the Lord—the silver from each man included in the census, and all the silver that anyone feels moved to bring into the house of the Lord—
let the priests take for themselves, each from his own sales, and let them repair the damage to the house of the Lord wherever damage is found.”
But in the twenty-third year of King Joash, the priests had not repaired the damage to the house of the Lord.

King Joash summoned Jehoiada the priest and the other priests and said to them, “Why have you not repaired the damage to the house of the Lord? Now take no more silver from any of your sales, but give it toward repairing the damage to the house of the Lord.”
The priests agreed not to take silver from the people and not to repair the damage to the house.
Jehoiada the priest took a chest, bored a hole in its lid, and placed it beside the altar of the Lord. The priests who guarded the entrance put into it all the silver found in the house of the Lord.
Whenever they saw that there was a large amount in the chest, the royal secretary and the high priest came up and bundled the silver found in the house of the Lord.
They handed the prepared silver over to those doing the work on the furnishings of the house of the Lord, and they gave it to the carpenters and builders working in the house of the Lord,
and to the painters, craftsmen, and stonecutters, to supply timber and dressed stones for repairing the damage to the house of the Lord, and for every expense incurred in repairing the house.
But no silver doors, nails, basins, trumpets, or any gold or silver vessels were to be made for the house of the Lord from the silver brought into the house of the Lord.
Instead, they were to give it to the workers, who would repair the house of the Lord.
They did not require an accounting from the men into whose hands they gave the silver to pay the workers, because they acted faithfully.
The silver for sins and offenses was not brought into the house of the Lord; it belonged to the priests.
Then Hazael king of Aram went up, fought against Gath, and captured it. Hazael then set his face toward going up against Jerusalem.

Joash king of Judah took all the sacred offerings dedicated by Jehoshaphat, Jehoram, and Ahaziah, his ancestors and kings of Judah, together with his own sacred offerings and all the silver found in the treasuries of the house of the Lord and the king’s house. He sent them to Hazael king of Aram, who then withdrew from Jerusalem.
As for the rest of the deeds of Joash and everything he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
His servants rose up, formed a conspiracy against him, and struck down Joash in the house of Maalon, situated in Gilead.
Jozacar son of Jemuath and Jezebuth his son, [?], his servants, struck him down and killed him. They buried him with his ancestors in the City of David, and his son Amaziah became king in his place.
In the twenty-third year of Joash son of Ahaziah, king of Judah, Jehoahaz son of Jehu became king over Israel in Samaria and reigned for seventeen years.
He did evil before the Lord and followed the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin. He did not turn away from them.
The Lord’s anger burned against Israel, and he continually delivered them into the hands of Hazael king of Aram and into the hands of Ben-hadad son of Hazael.
Jehoahaz sought the Lord’s favor, and the Lord listened to him, for he saw the oppression of Israel, whom the king of Aram had oppressed.
The Lord gave Israel a deliverer, and they escaped from the hands of the Arameans. The Israelites lived in their own dwellings as they had before.
Nevertheless, they did not turn away from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who had led Israel into sin, but continued in them. The sacred grove also remained in Samaria.
No army was left to Jehoahaz except fifty horsemen, ten chariots, and ten thousand foot soldiers, because the king of Syria had destroyed them and made them like dust to be trampled underfoot.
As for the rest of the deeds of Jehoahaz, everything he did, and his mighty deeds, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?
Jehoahaz slept with his ancestors, and they buried him with his ancestors in Samaria. His son Joash became king in his place.
In the thirty-seventh year of Joash king of Judah, Joash son of Jehoahaz became king over Israel in Samaria and reigned for twelve years.
He did evil in the sight of the Lord and did not turn away from any of the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who had led Israel into sin, but continued in them.
As for the rest of the deeds of Joash, everything he did, and his mighty deeds against the king of Judah, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?
Joash slept with his ancestors, and Jeroboam sat on his throne. Joash was buried in Samaria with the kings of Israel.
Elisha became sick with the illness from which he died. Joash king of Israel went down to him, wept over his face, and said, “Father, father! The chariots of Israel and its horsemen!”
Elisha said to him, “Take your bow and your arrows.” And he took the bow and the arrows.
He said to the king of Israel, “Put your hands on the bow.” He put his hands on the bow, and Elisha placed his hand over the king’s hands.

He said, “Open the window facing east.” And he opened it. Elisha said, “Shoot!” And he shot. Then he said, “An arrow of the Lord’s deliverance, an arrow of deliverance against the Syrians! You will strike the Syrians at Aphek until they are utterly destroyed.”
Elisha said to him, “Take the arrows.” And he took them. He said to the king of Israel, “Shoot and strike the ground.” The king struck three times and stopped.

The man of God was displeased with him and said, “If you had struck five or six times, then you would have struck the Syrians until they were utterly destroyed. But now you will strike the Syrians three times.”
Elisha died, and they buried him. Moabite raiding bands entered the land at the beginning of the year.
As they were burying a man, they saw the raiders and threw the man into Elisha’s tomb. The man moved and touched Elisha’s bones, came to life, and stood on his feet.
Hazael king of Syria oppressed Israel throughout the days of Jehoahaz.

But the Lord showed them mercy, had compassion on them, and looked upon them because of his covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. The Lord was unwilling to destroy them and did not cast them out of his presence.
Hazael king of Syria died, and his son Ben-hadad became king in his place.
Joash son of Jehoahaz took back from Ben-hadad son of Hazael the cities that he had taken from his father Jehoahaz in war. Joash defeated him three times and restored the cities to Israel.
In the second year of Joash son of Jehoahaz, king of Israel, Amaziah son of Joash became king of Judah.
He was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Jehoaddan, from Jerusalem.
He did what was right in the sight of the Lord, but not as David his ancestor had done. He did everything as his father Joash had done.
But he did not remove the high places, and the people still sacrificed and burned incense at the high places.
When the kingdom was firmly established in his hands, he struck down his servants who had struck down the king, his father.

But he did not kill the sons of the murderers, as it is written in the book of the Law of Moses, according to what the Lord commanded: “Fathers must not be put to death for their sons, nor must sons be put to death for their fathers. Instead, each person must die for his own sin.”
He struck down ten thousand Edomites at Maela, captured Sela in battle, and named it Joktheel, its name to this day.
At that time Amaziah sent messengers to Joash son of Jehoahaz, son of Jehu, king of Israel, saying, “Come, let us face one another.”

Joash king of Israel sent word to Amaziah king of Judah, saying, “The thistle in Lebanon sent word to the fir tree in Lebanon, saying, ‘Give your daughter to my son as his wife.’ But the wild beasts in Lebanon passed by and trampled the thistle.”
“You have indeed defeated Edom, and your heart has made you proud. Enjoy your glory and stay at home. Why should your wickedness provoke you, so that you fall, and Judah with you?”
But Amaziah would not listen. Joash, king of Israel, went up, and he and Amaziah, king of Judah, faced one another at Beth-shemesh in Judah.
Judah was defeated before Israel, and each man fled to his own home.

Joash son of Jehoahaz, king of Israel, captured Amaziah king of Judah, son of Joash, son of Ahaziah, at Beth-shemesh. He came to Jerusalem and tore down four hundred cubits of Jerusalem’s wall, from the Gate of Ephraim to the Corner Gate.
He took the gold, the silver, and all the vessels found in the house of the Lord and in the treasuries of the king’s house, as well as the hostages, and returned to Samaria.
The rest of the deeds of Joash, what he accomplished by his might, and the war he fought against Amaziah king of Judah—are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
Joash rested with his ancestors and was buried in Samaria with the kings of Israel. His son Jeroboam became king in his place.
Amaziah son of Joash, king of Judah, lived for fifteen years after the death of Joash son of Jehoahaz, king of Israel.
As for the rest of Amaziah’s deeds and everything he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
Bands gathered against him in Jerusalem, and he fled to Lachish. They sent men after him to Lachish and killed him there.
They carried him on horses, and he was buried in Jerusalem with his fathers in the City of David.
All the people of Judah took Azariah, who was sixteen years old, and made him king in place of his father Amaziah.
He rebuilt Elath and restored it to Judah after the king had rested with his fathers.
In the fifteenth year of Amaziah son of Joash, king of Judah, Jeroboam son of Joash, king of Israel, began to reign over Israel in Samaria, and he reigned for forty-one years.
He did evil before the Lord and did not turn away from any of the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin.

He pushed back the boundaries of Israel from the entrance of Hamath to the Sea of the Arabah, according to the word of the Lord, the God of Israel, which he spoke through his servant Jonah son of Amittai, the prophet from Gath-hepher.
For the Lord saw Israel’s extremely bitter suffering: they were few in number, oppressed, weakened, and abandoned, and there was no one to help Israel.
The Lord had not said that he would wipe out Israel’s descendants from under heaven, and the Lord saved them through Jeroboam son of Joash.

The rest of the deeds of Jeroboam, everything he did, his mighty deeds in war, and how he restored Damascus and Hamath to Judah from Israel—are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
Jeroboam rested with his fathers, with the kings of Israel, and his son Zechariah became king in place of his father.
In the twenty-seventh year of Jeroboam king of Israel, Azariah son of Amaziah, king of Judah, began to reign.
He was sixteen years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem for fifty-two years. His mother’s name was Jecoliah, from Jerusalem.
He did what was right in the sight of the Lord, just as his father Amaziah had done in everything.
But he did not remove the high places, and the people still offered sacrifices and burned incense at the high places.

The Lord struck the king, and he was a leper until the day of his death. He lived in the house of Apphusoth, while Jotham, the king’s son, was in charge of the palace and judged the people of the land.
Now the rest of the deeds of Azariah, and everything he did, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah?
Azariah slept with his ancestors, and they buried him beside his ancestors in the city of David. His son Jotham became king in his place.
In the thirty-eighth year of Azariah king of Judah, Zechariah son of Jeroboam became king over Israel in Samaria, and he reigned for six months.
He did what was evil in the sight of the Lord, as his ancestors had done. He did not turn away from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin.
Shallum son of Jabesh and Kebdaam conspired against him. They struck him down in front of the people and killed him, and Shallum became king in his place.
Now the rest of the deeds of Zechariah are written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel.
This was the word of the Lord that he spoke to Jehu, saying, “Your descendants to the fourth generation shall sit on the throne of Israel.” And so it happened.
Shallum son of Jabesh became king in the thirty-ninth year of Azariah king of Judah, and Shallum reigned in Samaria for one month.
Menahem son of Gadi went up from Tirzah and entered Samaria. He struck down Shallum son of Jabesh in Samaria and killed him, and became king in his place.
Now the rest of the deeds of Shallum, and the conspiracy he carried out, are written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel.
At that time Menahem attacked Tiphsah, everyone in it, and its territory from Tirzah, because they did not open their gates to him. He struck it down and ripped open its pregnant women.
In the thirty-ninth year of Azariah king of Judah, Menahem son of Gadi became king over Israel in Samaria, and he reigned for ten years.
He did what was evil in the sight of the Lord and did not turn away from any of the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin through his own sins.
Pul king of Assyria came against the land, and Menahem gave Pul a thousand talents of silver so that he would support him and establish the kingdom in his hands.
Menahem levied the silver on Israel, on all the men of wealth, to give to the king of Assyria: fifty shekels of silver from each man. Then the king of Assyria withdrew and did not remain in the land.
Now the rest of the deeds of Menahem, and everything he did, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?
Menahem slept with his ancestors, and his son Pekahiah became king in his place.
In the fiftieth year of Azariah king of Judah, Pekahiah became king over Israel in Samaria, and he reigned for ten years.
He did what was evil in the sight of the Lord and did not turn away from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin.

Pekah son of Remaliah, his armor-bearer, conspired against him and struck him down in Samaria in front of the king’s palace. With him were Argob and Arieh, and with him were fifty men from the four hundred. He killed him and became king in his place.
Now the rest of the deeds of Pekahiah, and everything he did, are written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel.
In the fifty-second year of Azariah king of Judah, Pekah son of Remaliah became king over Israel in Samaria and reigned for twenty years.
He did evil before the Lord and did not turn away from any of the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin.

In the days of Pekah king of Israel, Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria came and captured Ain, Kabel, Beth-maacah, Janoah, Kenaz, Hazor, Gilead, Galilee, and all the land of Naphtali, and deported their inhabitants to Assyria.
Hoshea son of Elah gathered a band against Pekah son of Remaliah, struck him down and killed him, and became king in his place in the twentieth year of Jotham son of Uzziah.
The rest of the acts of Pekah and everything he did are recorded in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel.
In the second year of Pekah son of Remaliah king of Israel, Jotham son of Uzziah king of Judah became king.
He was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem for sixteen years. His mother's name was Jerusha, daughter of Zadok.
He did what was right before the Lord, in accordance with everything his father Uzziah had done.
But he did not remove the high places, and the people still sacrificed and burned incense at the high places. He built the Upper Gate of the house of the Lord.
The rest of the acts of Jotham and everything he did—are they not recorded in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
In those days the Lord began to send Rezin king of Syria and Pekah son of Remaliah against Judah.
Jotham rested with his ancestors and was buried with his ancestors in the city of David his ancestor. His son Ahaz became king in his place.
In the seventeenth year of Pekah son of Remaliah, Ahaz son of Jotham king of Judah became king.
Ahaz was twenty years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem for sixteen years. He did not faithfully do what was right before the Lord God, as his ancestor David had done.
He followed the way of Jeroboam son of Nebat, king of Israel. He even made his son pass through fire, following the abominations of the nations whom the Lord had driven out before the Israelites.
He sacrificed and burned incense at the high places, on the hills, and beneath densely leafy trees.
Then Rezin king of Syria and Pekah son of Remaliah king of Israel went up to Jerusalem to wage war. They besieged it against Ahaz, but they were unable to fight.
At that time Rezin king of Syria restored Elath to Syria and drove the Jews out of Elath. The Edomites came to Elath and settled there, where they remain to this day.

Ahaz sent messengers to Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria, saying, "I am your servant and your son. Come up and save me from the hand of the king of Syria and from the hand of the king of Israel, who have risen against me."
Ahaz took the silver and gold found in the house of the Lord and in the treasuries of the king's house, and sent gifts to the king of Assyria.
The king of Assyria listened to him. The king of Assyria went up to Damascus, captured it, deported its inhabitants to Cyrene, and killed Rezin.

King Ahaz went to Damascus to meet Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria. He saw the altar in Damascus, and King Ahaz sent Uriah the priest a likeness of the altar and its design, showing all its workmanship.
Uriah the priest built the altar in accordance with everything King Ahaz had sent from Damascus. Uriah the priest completed it in this way before King Ahaz returned from Damascus.
He saw the altar, and the king approached the altar and went up onto it.
He burned his burnt offerings and his sacrifices, presented his offerings, and poured out the blood of his peace offerings.
He moved the bronze altar that stood before the Lord from its place in front of the Lord’s house and put it on the north side of the altar.

King Ahaz gave orders to Uriah the priest, saying, “On this great altar you shall offer the morning burnt offerings and the evening sacrifices, the king’s burnt offerings and his sacrifices, and the burnt offerings of the people of this land, their sacrifices, and their offerings. You shall pour all the blood of the burnt offerings and all the blood of the sacrifices on it. But the bronze altar shall be for me in the mornings.”
Uriah the priest did everything just as King Ahaz had commanded him.
King Ahaz cut away the fittings of the stands and removed the basins from them. He lowered the Sea from the twelve bronze bulls beneath it and set it on a stone base.
He built the foundation of the throne in the Lord’s house and turned the king’s outer entrance toward the Lord’s house because of the king of Assyria.
As for the rest of the deeds of Ahaz, what he did, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah?
Ahaz rested with his ancestors and was buried with his ancestors in the City of David. His son Hezekiah became king in his place.
In the twelfth year of Ahaz king of Judah, Hoshea son of Elah became king over Israel in Samaria, and he reigned for nine years.
He did evil before the Lord, but not like the kings of Israel who were before him.
Shalmaneser king of Assyria came up against him, and Hoshea became his servant and sent him tribute.

The king of Assyria discovered treachery in Hoshea, because he had sent messengers to So king of Egypt and had not given tribute to the king of Assyria that year. The king of Assyria confined him and bound him in prison.
The king of Assyria advanced through the whole land. He also advanced against Samaria and besieged it for three years.
In the ninth year of Hoshea, the king of Assyria captured Samaria and deported Israel to Assyria. He settled them in Halah and in Habor, by the river of Gozan, and in the mountains of the Medes.
And it happened that the Israelites sinned against the Lord their God, who had brought them out of the land of Egypt, out of the hands of Pharaoh king of Egypt, and they feared foreign gods
and followed the customs of the nations whom the Lord had removed from before the Israelites.

And the kings of Israel did whatever they did, and the Israelites made up things about the Lord their God that were not true. They built high places for themselves in all their cities, from the watchtower to the fortified city.
They set up pillars and sacred groves for themselves on every high hill and beneath every leafy tree
and burned incense at all the high places, like all the nations whom the Lord had driven out from before them. They made [?] and acted wickedly to provoke the Lord
and worshiped idols, concerning which the Lord had told them, “Do not do this thing to the Lord.”

The Lord warned Israel and Judah through all his prophets and all the seers, saying, “Turn back from your evil ways and keep my commandments, my statutes, and all the laws that I commanded your ancestors and sent to you through my servants the prophets.”
But they did not listen, and they made their necks stiffer than the necks of their ancestors, who did not believe in the Lord their God.

And they cast aside their statutes and the covenant that he had made with their fathers, and they did not keep his testimonies that he had enjoined upon them. They followed worthless things and became worthless, following the nations around them, concerning whom the Lord had commanded them not to follow their example.
They abandoned all the commandments of the Lord their God and made for themselves two cast-metal calves. They worshiped the host of heaven and served Baal.
And they made their sons and daughters pass through fire, practiced divination, cast spells, and dared to do evil before the Lord, provoking him to anger.
And the Lord became very angry with Israel and rejected them from his presence. None remained except the tribe of Judah alone.
Yet Judah also did not keep the commandments of the Lord their God, but followed the practices that Israel had established.
And they rejected the Lord from among all the descendants of Israel, and he shook them and delivered them into the hands of their plunderers, until he cast them out of his presence.
But Israel, [?] the house of David itself, made Jeroboam son of Nebat king. And Jeroboam turned Israel away from walking in the Lord’s ways and caused them to commit great sins.
And the children of Israel committed all the sins that Jeroboam had committed, and they did not turn away from them.
Until the Lord removed Israel from his presence, just as the Lord had spoken through all his servants the prophets. And Israel was carried away from its land to Assyria, where it remains to this day.

And the king of Assyria brought people from Babylon, Cuthah, Avva, Hamath, and Sepharvaim, and they settled in the cities of Samaria in place of the children of Israel. They took possession of Samaria and lived in its cities.
And when they first settled there, they did not fear the Lord. And the Lord sent lions, which killed them.

And they spoke to the king of Assyria, saying, “The nations whom you moved and settled in the cities of Samaria in place of the former inhabitants do not know the customs of the God of the land. The Lord has sent lions among them, and now they are killing them, because they do not know the customs of the God of the land.”

And the king of Assyria gave an order, saying, “Take one of the priests deported from there back there, so that he may go and live there, teach the customs of the Lord, and instruct them in the ordinances of the God of the land.”
And they took one of the priests whom they had deported from Samaria, and he settled in Bethel and taught them to fear the Lord.
And each nation made its own gods and placed them in the shrines at the high places that the Samaritans had made, each nation in its own cities where it lived.
And the people of Babylon made Succoth-benoth, the people of Cuthah made Nergal, and the people of Hamath made Ashima.
And the Avvites made Ablazer, Nibhaz, and Tartak; and Sepharvaim, where they burned their sons in fire to Adrammelech and Anammelech, the gods of Sepharvaim.

And they feared the Lord and installed their abominations in the shrines at the high places that they had made in Samaria, each nation where it lived. And they feared the Lord and appointed priests of the high places for themselves.
And they feared the Lord and served their own gods according to the customs of the nations whom God had driven out of there.

And to this day they continued to act according to their customs. They feared the Lord and acted according to their customs, their ordinances, the laws, and the commandment that the Lord had commanded the children of Jacob, whom he named Israel.
And the Lord made a covenant and commanded them, saying, “Do not fear foreign gods, do not bow down to them, do not serve them, and do not offer sacrifices to them.
Rather, fear the Lord God, who brought you out of the land of the Egyptians with great power and an uplifted arm. Bow down to him and offer sacrifices to him.
Be careful to carry out the ordinances, judgments, laws, and commandments that he wrote for you, and do not fear foreign gods.
Do not break the covenant that he made with you, and do not fear foreign gods.
But you shall fear the Lord your God, and he will deliver you from all your enemies.
And do not heed the religious practices that they observe.”
Those nations feared the Lord but also served their own carved idols. Their children and their grandchildren continue to do as their ancestors did, to this day.
In the third year of Hoshea son of Elah, king of Israel, Hezekiah son of Ahaz, king of Judah, became king.
He was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem for twenty-nine years. His mother’s name was Abi, the daughter of Zechariah.
He did what was right before the Lord, in accordance with everything that his ancestor David had done.

He removed the high places, shattered all the pillars, and destroyed the groves and the bronze serpent that Moses had made, because until those days the children of Israel had offered sacrifices to it. They called it Nehushtan.
He trusted in the Lord God of Israel. Among all the kings of Judah, there was no one like him after him or among those who had come before him.
He held fast to the Lord and did not depart from his ways. He kept the commandments that the Lord had commanded Moses.
The Lord was with him, and he acted wisely in everything he did. He rebelled against the king of Assyria and did not serve him.
He struck down the Philistines as far as Gaza and its territory, from the watchtower to the fortified city.
In the fourth year of King Hezekiah, which was the seventh year of Hoshea son of Elah, king of Israel, Shalmaneser king of Assyria came up against Samaria and besieged it.
He captured it at the end of three years. Samaria was captured in the sixth year of Hezekiah, which was the ninth year of Hoshea king of Israel.
The king of Assyria deported the people of Samaria to Assyria and settled them in Halah and Habor, by the river of Gozan, and in the mountains of the Medes.
For they did not obey the voice of the Lord their God, but violated his covenant. They neither listened to nor carried out all that Moses, the Lord’s servant, had commanded them.
In the fourteenth year of King Hezekiah, Sennacherib king of Assyria came up against the strongly fortified cities of Judah and captured them.

Hezekiah king of Judah sent messengers to the king of Assyria at Lachish, saying, “I have sinned. Withdraw from me, and I will bear whatever you impose on me.” The king of Assyria imposed on Hezekiah king of Judah three hundred talents of silver and thirty talents of gold.
